Node.js

You might say

The terminal says command not found: node. Why can't my project run?

A runtime for JavaScript outside the browser, often used by local scripts and build tools·When a project specifies a Node.js version, use node -v in the terminal to check your local runtime. Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser and can provide local capabilities such as file-system access; browser scripts run in a page environment, which is different.
Know first
JavaScript
Nodenode
The same .js file, run by a browser and by Node.js
script.js
const fs = require("fs");
const files = fs.readdirSync("./data");
console.log(`Read ${files.length} files`);
→
file:///Users/you/project/script.js
const fs = require("fs");
const files = fs.readdirSync("./data");
console.log(`Read ${files.length} files`);
The browser just shows the file as text; it does not run it

JavaScript commonly runs in browser pages or in Node.js in a terminal. npm runs on Node.js, and many project build commands use it; requirements depend on the toolchain.

Where Node.js sits in the toolchain

It is a runtime, not a new language: You still write JavaScript. Node.js adds the ability to execute it on a computer, so scripts run without opening a browser.

Build and package tools depend on it: npm and many project build commands use Node.js; whether a project needs it depends on its toolchain. Commands that rely on a missing Node.js installation report command not found.

Projects require specific versions: When docs say requires Node 18+, run node -v to see the local version; upgrade before running if it is too low.

What it does not replace

Node.js does not replace the browser: in-page interactions still run there. It adds the ability to run JavaScript outside the browser, which command-line tools and server programs rely on.
